newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks fall on lower dollar.
newsitem.headline: French stocks fall on lower dollar.

text.p: French stocks opened lower on Monday after the dollar slipped against European currencies, brokers said.
They said investors were concerned about the volatility of the markets and trade was likely to be cautious ahead of U.S. housing starts on Tuesday and inflation data on Wednesday.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index down 23.71 points, or 0.9 percent, at 2,621.91 at 0935 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was 14 points lower at 2,626.

Shares in Lyonnaise des Eaux were up 0.17 percent at 581 francs. The chairman of its Elyo subsidiary predicted a rise of more than 20 percent, and perhaps even 30 percent, in 1997 net attributable profit, due to restructuring gains.
Shares in tyremaker Michelin were up 1.2 percent ahead of its 1996 results due on Tuesday.
Shares in Elf Sanofi rose 0.55 percent at 547 francs, buoyed by a report in the weekly newsletter Lettre de L'Expansion of a possible alliance with Parke-Davis. Sanofi declined to comment.
